clue.text: Airport sign I follow — welcoming English sign

indicators.note: welcoming means one piece takes another in, so the English letter goes within

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
the Ram is Aries, a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone at an airport follows a sign that welcomes English travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' makes the dog take in E, giving DEOG. The second 'sign' is Aries, the zodiac Ram; airport signs are pictures standing for ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Airport signage uses pictorial symbols standing for ideas, which is exactly what this kind of written character is.

clue.text: From Land's End sail away to Island Republic

indicators.note: End picks the final letter of the word Land's

parts.note: a jib is a triangular sail
out means away, as in out of the office

explanation.surface: A voyage setting off from the tip of Cornwall bound for an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the far western tip of Cornwall in England.
explanation.definitionFit: This small Horn of Africa state is a republic on the Gulf of Aden.

clue.text: All-powerful men with point to make, possibly

indicators.note: make, possibly suggests the letters could be made into something else, an arrangement signal

explanation.surface: Men with a point to make feel they can do anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make, possibly' rearranges the ten letters of MEN, POINT and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnipotent means having unlimited power, a word often used of a deity.

clue.text: Pick up circular offering support

parts.note: to rally is to recover or improve, as markets do
round means circular in shape

explanation.surface: Someone collects a leaflet that offers help.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to gather to help someone in difficulty.

clue.text: Fellow's son picked up a Buddhist design

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: picked up means lifted, so in a down clue the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a lad is a son or boy

explanation.surface: A man's son lifts a piece of Buddhist art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns LAD to DAL in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This circular geometric pattern symbolises the universe in Buddhist and Hindu practice.

clue.text: Short life of current resident in Slough

indicators.note: resident in means living within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a slough is a bog or marsh
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A brief biography of someone living in the English town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the Berkshire town near London; here it is a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the informal abbreviation of biography, a written life story.

clue.text: May person, say, getting upset put on something to wear?

indicators.note: put on means placed above, so this piece sits on top of the next
upset means overturned, so in a down clue the letters go upwards

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: Someone born in spring gets upset trying on clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' turns EG upwards to GE in this down answer. Gemini is the star sign of people born from late May to late June.
explanation.definitionFit: People born from late May to June have the zodiac sign of the Twins.

clue.text: Suppress line? What's unusual about that?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the odd word goes round the other piece

parts.note: strange means unusual or odd

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a remark should be stifled and what is odd about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts STRANGE around L.
explanation.definitionFit: To choke something off, such as a cry or a laugh, is to stifle or suppress it.

clue.text: Ultimate proof of drug taken before match

indicators.note: taken before says the drug comes ahead of the match in the answer

parts.note: acid is slang for the drug LSD
a test is an international match, as in cricket's Test matches

explanation.surface: A sports report: an athlete takes drugs before a big game, and is caught.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a decisive trial that settles a question, originally the acid used to prove gold.

clue.text: Extraordinary gesture

definitions.meaning: as an adjective the word means remarkable, as in a notable victory
a movement or sign meant to convey a message

explanation.surface: A bare comment on some remarkable movement of the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means notable or striking; as a noun it is a sign made with the hand.

clue.text: Gladly avoid one left abandoned at sea — a barely recognised figure

indicators.note: at sea means confused or jumbled, so the remaining letters are rearranged
abandoned says the named letter is dropped from the fodder

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left, and only one of the two goes

explanation.surface: Someone happily avoids being left alone on a ship far out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' drops one L from GLADLY AVOID, and 'at sea' rearranges the ten letters left. Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry, so she was barely recognised in both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary noblewoman rode naked through Coventry, a figure seen only in the bare.

clue.text: Closely follow old writer

parts.note: to hug a coastline or a car is to keep very close behind or beside it

explanation.surface: Advice to stick close behind some elderly author.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor Hugo was the French author of Les Misérables.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor of that surname was the nineteenth-century French novelist and poet.

clue.text: Very lively and amusing lecture

definitions.meaning: exuberantly cheerful, as in a boisterous adventure story
a reprimand, as when a teacher scolds a pupil at length

explanation.surface: A description of a talk that was both energetic and funny.
explanation.walkthrough: In British informal use a 'rollicking' is a scolding, so 'lecture' is a second meaning, not part of the description.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes boisterous fun, and in British slang it is also a severe telling-off.

clue.text: Labour's leader overcome by disease and stress

indicators.note: leader picks the opening letter of the word Labour's

explanation.surface: The head of the Labour Party falls ill with stress.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is a British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: In speech, a change in pitch or emphasis on a syllable is a modulation of stress.

clue.text: King and I sets make cracking musical

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess

indicators.note: cracking means breaking apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.definitionFit: This Cole Porter show is a stage musical based on The Taming of the Shrew.

clue.text: Ghastly retreat, second for tommies at the front

indicators.note: for says one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: a hideout is a secret place to retreat to

indicators.note: at the front picks the opening letter of the word tommies

explanation.surface: British soldiers find their front-line retreat a ghastly place.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of HIDEOUT, the first letter of 'tommies', is replaced by S. Tommies are British soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something horribly ugly or repulsive to look at.

clue.text: Husband means to accept plan for den

indicators.note: to accept means taking in, so one piece goes inside the others

parts.note: a way is a means or method
an idea is a plan

explanation.surface: A husband finds ways to agree to plans for his study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' means the husband-plus-means pair takes the plan inside, so it splits after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A secluded spot where one can retreat unseen is a den or bolt-hole.

clue.text: Illegal position after run down wing?

parts.note: feeling off means unwell or below par, much like feeling run down
a side or wing is a flank of a team or building

explanation.surface: A football winger sprints down the flank and is flagged by the linesman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a winger flagged for straying ahead of the defenders, which is the meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In football or rugby, being ahead of the ball or the last defender is an infringement with this name.

clue.text: People go slowly at first in driving speed test

clue.text: China holds one short poll that's decisive

clue.text: Anticipating employment, woman and man sign on here

indicators.note: anticipating means coming before, so the two names precede the job word

one's line is one's job or occupation, as in 'what's your line?'

explanation.surface: A couple are about to start work and are told where to sign the contract.

clue.text: Artist being terribly intimate? Not with me, being separated!

parts.note: taken as written, letters removed from the pool

explanation.definitionFit: Tiziano Vecellio was the great Venetian Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Royal address approached from east or west

indicators.note: approached from either end, the letters read identically in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone bows to a queen whichever side they come at her from.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters read the same left to right and right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: This contraction of madam is how one properly addresses the Queen after the first 'Your Majesty'.

clue.text: Fool about to get at chap almost drunk

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before its end is cut

explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts CHAP to CHA, which joins TO GET AT; 'drunk' rearranges the ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to behave in a silly, playful way, a British informal phrase for clowning around.

clue.text: Flyer heading off from capital of Europe

clue.text: A prisoner inside with a South American killer

taken as written

clue.text: Like very observant person to join team on radio
